hardware: AMD Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 (Strix Halo, ~220 GB/s achievable LPDDR5X)
purpose: AR decode profile - the untouched multiplier (MTP tok/s = AR x uplift). Identifies where AR decode bandwidth headroom is, as a correctness-preserving path to lift absolute MTP tok/s toward llama parity.
finding: lm-head q6_k GEMV is already near peak BW (~217 GB/s; 413MB/1.9ms) - efficient. The q8_0 attention-projection GEMVs aggregate ~42% of AR at only ~53 GB/s (~25% of peak): small-output (256-2048), latency-bound, under-parallelized single-token GEMVs. This is the real correctness-preserving AR headroom.
path_to_parity: AR 54.6 x uplift 1.114 = 60.8 (current). Matching llama 67.3 needs AR ~60.4 (a ~10.6% AR speedup) at constant uplift, since faster AR kernels also speed the verify. Optimizing the latency-bound q8_0 attention-projection GEMVs (split-K / higher occupancy / q/k/v fusion) is the target. CAVEAT: small-batch GEMV is latency-floored; hipEngine AR already beats llama AR (54.6 vs 50.1), so this is hard central kernel R&D, not config. Realistic gain uncertain (10-20% on those kernels -> ~5-8% AR).
